source: no published source; read from the installed 2.0.0 build

lines: Two sixteen-step binary words, set bit by bit with the buttons and played out a bit at a time, each word giving a held level and a trigger, with a chance of any bit coming out random instead

Sets the internal clock rate, doubling it for every 1 the knob adds and starting at 10Hz; the readout gives that exponent rather than the frequency, so it says 3.322 where the clock is running at 10Hz
Scales the voltage at the clock rate jack, and turns it upside down below the centre; with it centred that jack does nothing
Chooses whether the sequence steps from the module's own clock or from the voltage at CLK IN, printing Internal and External
Sets how many of the sixteen bits are played before the word starts again, 1 to 16
Chooses whether the two words play side by side as sixteen bits each or end to end as thirty-two, printing 16 bit and 32 bit
Restarts the word at its first bit and plays one cycle, then stops on the last bit
Chooses whether the sequence keeps repeating or runs one cycle at a time, printing Auto and Single; on Single nothing moves until the button is pressed or a trigger arrives
Sets the chance, drawn afresh for every bit on every cycle, that the bit played comes from a pseudo-random word instead of the one the buttons set; at the bottom of its travel only the buttons count
Turns every bit of the first word over, so a button switched off plays a one and a button switched on plays a zero
Turns every bit of the second word over, so a button switched off plays a one and a button switched on plays a zero
Sets that bit of the first word on or off, and the lamp beside it shows the bit actually played, which is not the same thing once the invert switch or the random chance is in play
Sets that bit of the second word on or off, and the lamp beside it shows the bit actually played, which is not the same thing once the invert switch or the random chance is in play
Moves the internal clock rate, scaled by the attenuverter beside it, and 5V at full attenuation doubles the rate
Adds to the word length at one and a half bits per volt, rounded to a whole bit, with the total held between 1 and 16
A trigger restarts the word at its first bit and plays one cycle; it fires above 1V and rearms below 0V
A trigger flips the 16 bit and 32 bit switch itself, so the switch on the panel moves; it fires above 1V and rearms below 0V
Adds to the random-chance knob, where 10V covers the whole of that knob's travel
One step of the sequence for every rise above 1V, and only while the clock switch is on External
A trigger sends the sequence back to its first bit and draws a fresh pseudo-random word for the random-chance setting to use; it fires above 1V and rearms below 0V
A trigger flips the first word's invert switch itself, so the switch on the panel moves; it fires above 1V and rearms below 0V
A trigger flips the second word's invert switch itself, so the switch on the panel moves; it fires above 1V and rearms below 0V
10V for the whole step while the first word's current bit is on and 0V while it is off, which is a gate rather than the control voltage the panel calls it
A 1ms 10V pulse on each step where the first word's current bit is on, which is a trigger rather than the gate the panel calls it
10V for the whole step while the second word's current bit is on and 0V while it is off, which is a gate rather than the control voltage the panel calls it
A 1ms 10V pulse on each step where the second word's current bit is on, which is a trigger rather than the gate the panel calls it
The clock the sequence is running on: a square wave at the rate the CLOCK knob sets, half the time at 10V, or a copy of whatever is at CLK IN when the clock switch is on External
A 1ms 10V pulse as the sequence reaches the first bit of the word
A 1ms 10V pulse as the sequence reaches the last bit of the word
Note — on 32 bit the words play end to end and the cycle doubles, but the two outputs differ: the first word's output runs A then B while the second's runs B then A, sixteen steps apart
Note — WORD LEN counts bits in one word, so on 32 bit a length of 16 gives a cycle of 32 steps
Note — the module comes up with every bit button off, clock Internal, Auto, 16 bit, length 16 and no random chance, so it clocks along with both words silent until you switch some bits on
Note — the panel prints BOOGA WORD GENERATOR and the module is modelled on the HP 8006A word generator, a bench instrument for feeding a digital circuit a chosen pattern of ones and zeros

0.why: process at 0x6514 reads inputs[0].voltages[0] only when the clock switch reads External, and 0x6520-0x6608 runs it through a three-state edge test that arms above 1.0 and rearms at or below 0.0

1.why: process at 0x61d8 reads inputs[1].voltages[0] and runs it through the same three-state edge test against 1.0 and 0.0

2.why: process at 0x6268 reads inputs[2].voltages[0] and runs it through the same three-state edge test against 1.0 and 0.0

3.why: process at 0x6694 reads inputs[3].voltages[0] only when the port is connected, multiplies it by 0.1, adds it to the PRN knob at 0x66b4 and clamps the sum to 0 and 1; nothing clamps or rectifies the voltage itself, only the sum, so the binary cannot separate a 0 to 10V jack from a ±5V one whose re-centring the compiler folded into the same multiply and add; no range is recorded for that reason

4.why: process at 0x60f8 reads inputs[4].voltages[0] through the same three-state edge test, and 0x6118 writes 1 minus the Invert Word A parameter back into that parameter

5.why: process at 0x617c reads inputs[5].voltages[0] through the same three-state edge test, and 0x6198 writes 1 minus the Invert Word B parameter back into that parameter

6.why: process at 0x5e78 reads inputs[6].voltages[0] only when the port is connected, multiplies it by 1.5, rounds to an integer, adds it to the word length and clamps the sum to 1 and 16; nothing clamps or rectifies the voltage itself, only the sum, so the binary cannot separate a 0 to 10V jack from a ±5V one whose re-centring the compiler folded into the same multiply and add; no range is recorded for that reason

7.why: process at 0x5eb0 reads inputs[7].voltages[0] through the same three-state edge test, and 0x5efc writes 1 minus the Mode parameter back into that parameter

8.why: process at 0x6570 reads inputs[8].voltages[0] only when the port is connected, multiplies it by 0.2 and then by the attenuverter, and adds the result to the rate knob before the clamp at 0x6598

0.why: process at 0x6a9c writes 10 or 0 into outputs[0].voltages[0] with no setChannels; the 10 lasts while a countdown set to 0.001 at 0x68e0 is still above zero

1.why: process at 0x6ac0 writes 10 or 0 into outputs[1].voltages[0] with no setChannels; the 10 lasts while a countdown set to 0.001 at 0x6900 is still above zero

2.why: process at 0x6a64 writes 10 or 0 into outputs[2].voltages[0] with no setChannels, chosen by the current bit of the first word, and the value is held until the next step

3.why: process at 0x6a74 writes 10 or 0 into outputs[3].voltages[0] with no setChannels, chosen by the current bit of the second word, and the value is held until the next step

4.why: process at 0x6aec writes 10 or 0 into outputs[4].voltages[0] with no setChannels; the countdown is set to 0.001 at 0x6920 when the step index is zero

5.why: process at 0x6b10 writes 10 or 0 into outputs[5].voltages[0] with no setChannels; the countdown is set to 0.001 at 0x6958 when the step index is the last of the cycle

6.why: process at 0x65f8 writes 10 or 0 into outputs[6].voltages[0] from the internal phase accumulator, half the cycle each; at 0x6638 it writes the clock input's own voltage through instead when the switch is on External

WordGenerator.notes: The maker publishes no source and gives no plugin, manual, source or changelog URL, so this was read out of the installed 2.0.0 binary: WordGenerator::process at 0x5e34, the constructor at 0x3d5c, and the three helpers generatePRN, advanceSequence and computeOutputByte. THE FOUR AUDIO-ISH OUTPUTS ARE NAMED THE WRONG WAY ROUND. The jacks the panel prints CV A and CV B hold 10V or 0V for the whole of a step, which is a gate; the jacks it prints GATE A and GATE B emit a 1ms pulse, which is a trigger. The code is unambiguous: outputs 2 and 3 are written from the bit value directly, outputs 0 and 1 from a countdown initialised to 0.001 seconds. SECOND FAULT, in a tooltip: the Clock Rate parameter is configured with a range of -3.321928 to 9.965784 and a default of 3.321928, which are log2 of 0.1, 1000 and 10, but with a display base of 0 and a unit of ' Hz', so Rack's readout shows the exponent labelled as a frequency. The 0.1Hz, 1000Hz and 10Hz figures are exact exp2 of constants that are in the binary rather than constants themselves, which is why a literal check will not find them. Both are called out in the lines. The switches are configSwitch with printed choices: Clock Mode gives Internal and External, Mode gives 16 bit and 32 bit, Run Mode gives Auto and Single. The two Invert switches and all thirty-two bit buttons are configSwitch with no choice names at all. Every trigger jack, the clock input included, uses the same hand-written three-state edge detector that arms above 1.0 and rearms at or below 0.0, not Rack's dsp::SchmittTrigger. The 16/32 and the two invert jacks write back into their own parameters, so a trigger visibly moves the switch on the panel; that also means the setting a patch reloads with is wherever the last trigger left it. PRN substitution is redrawn for all sixteen bit positions of both words at every step boundary using rack::random::local, and it is compared against the knob-plus-CV value once per bit, so a setting of 0.5 gives a different word every cycle. Reset reseeds a 32-bit LFSR from rack::random::local, falling back to 0xABCDEF12 when that returns a zero high word. The thirty-two lamps are fed the effective word, after inversion and after PRN substitution, so a lamp can disagree with the button under it. All nine inputs are read on channel 0 only and all seven outputs are written on channel 0 only; nothing in the module calls setChannels.
